result:
Round 31 (FB-05 track pan) is implemented and all the A-side gates pass on the current files; C still has to verify it, so I'm not marking any acceptance criterion as passed.

An earlier A session wrote the code, tests and doc but was cut off before finishing (its result file is empty, and the test file and doc changed after its last saved gate run). I made no code or doc changes. I re-ran every gate on the final files and added a section to the end of `a-round-31.md` recording that.

**Changed files** (exactly the 7 the task allows): `types/arrangement.ts`, `model.ts`, `graph.client.ts`, `ArrangementContext.tsx` and `ArrangementLane.tsx`, plus the new `track-pan.test.tsx` and doc 036. Before the change, all 26 new tests failed against the original sources.

**What I ran:**

Doc 036 is complete and matches the final code.

**Deviations B needs to accept:**
- **Stricter Pan refusal:** Pan changes are refused during any pointer gesture, including that track's own pan drag. Otherwise a reset clicked with a second pointer during a drag makes two history entries.
- **Delete/Backspace on the Pan slider:** they are stopped there, so they no longer delete a selected clip. The guard had to go on the slider because `StudioWorkspace.tsx` is frozen this round.
- **Other details:**
  - a release from a different pointer doesn't end the drag;
  - after a reset, focus moves to the Pan slider;
  - an invalid stored pan (NaN) plays as centre;
  - the model function is named `setArrangementTrackPan`;
  - the graph compares new values against the last value it set, not the read-back value.

**New bug for B (VOLUME-DELETE-KEY):** pressing Delete on a focused Volume slider deletes the selected clip. It already existed before this round. I didn't fix it because row 2 was frozen.

- The pan push in the playback-sync path is defensive. A mutation that only removes it may not make any test fail.
- Review finding #2 is left as is: in a rare case after an interrupted drag, the slider can briefly show a value that isn't stored. It clears on the next release or blur.
